reasoning: Roofline marks compute bottleneck with Compute SOL 60.8% vs Memory SOL 31.7%; NCU matches this (sm throughput 60.85% of peak, DRAM throughput 31.74%), so math pipelines are the dominant limiter rather than bandwidth.

root_causes.cause: No matrix-core/tensor-core usage, so matmul runs on VALU FP pipelines with lower effective peak.

evidence.interpretation: Tensor/matrix pipelines are completely inactive; compute work is not using fastest matmul units.

fixes.fix: Enable tensor-core/matrix-instruction paths in Triton (use fp16/bf16-friendly dot configuration and tile shapes known to map to MFMA on gfx942).
fixes.rationale: Shifting GEMM work from VALU to matrix units increases achievable compute throughput and raises the compute roof.

root_causes.cause: Current tiling/launch configuration leaves substantial compute headroom despite full warp activity.

evidence.interpretation: Only ~61% of peak SM throughput is reached, indicating execution efficiency limits in current schedule/tile choice.

fixes.fix: Retune autotune space toward larger K blocking and pipeline depth (e.g., more aggressive BLOCK_K/num_stages and candidate warp layouts) for this shape regime.
fixes.rationale: Better instruction-level reuse and scheduling can improve FMA issue efficiency and close the ~39% compute headroom.
